story_title: Lina and Adams and the Busy Street
title: Lina and Adams and the Busy Street 🚲 | Learn Street Words in English for Kids | Moon Tales Kids
description:
Walk down the busy street with Lina, Adams and Milo, and learn to stay safe! 🚗🚌🚲
In this English story for kids, children learn 8 new words: street, car, bus, bike, helmet, stop, go and slow. Listen, repeat, and learn English with Lina, Adams and Milo the cat.

📚 New words in this story:
🏙️ street — الشارع — la rue
🚗 car — السيارة — la voiture
🚌 bus — الحافلة — le bus
🚲 bike — الدراجة — le vélo
⛑️ helmet — الخوذة — le casque
🛑 stop — قف / توقف — stop / arrête-toi
🟢 go — انطلق / اذهب — vas-y / avance
🐢 slow — ببطء — lentement

👨‍👩‍👧 For parents: talk with your child about holding hands and stopping at the street. Pause after each new word and say it together. Perfect for ages 3 to 8 and for children learning English as a second language.

lines.text: It is a bright morning. Lina and Adams are eating breakfast.
Lina, today we go to the park with Mama!
Hooray! We will walk down the big street.
Milo the cat jumps on the chair. Meow!
Mama says: put on your shoes, and hold my hand outside.
Yes, Mama. We always hold hands near the street.
Meow! Me too!
Lina, Adams and Milo go outside with Mama.
Look, Adams! This is our street. It is long and busy.
I can see houses, and shops, and trees!
A street is a road in a town, with houses and shops next to it.
Say it with me: street!
Milo walks close to Lina's feet. He is a good cat.
Vroom, vroom! What is that sound?
Look, a red car! It has four round wheels.
The car goes on the road. We walk on the side.
A car takes people from one place to another.
Can you say it? Car!
Beep, beep! Bye bye, red car!
Then, a very big, yellow car comes down the street.
Adams, what is that? It is so long!
It is a bus! Many people ride on the bus.
The bus stops, and the doors open. Ding, ding!
A bus is a big car that carries many people.
Say it with me: bus!
Hello, bus driver! Have a nice day!
At the park, Adams sees his bike next to a tree.
My bike! Papa brought it for me this morning.
Your bike is blue, like your shirt!
A bike has two wheels. You push the pedals with your feet.
Let's say it together: bike!
Lina, you can ride my bike too. Let's share!
Adams wants to ride right now. But wait!
Adams! Where is your helmet?
Oh! I forgot. Here it is. I put it on my head.
A helmet is a strong hat. It keeps your head safe.
Say it with me: helmet!
Click! Now my helmet is on. I am ready!
Meow! Safe and ready!
Lina and Adams play with a ball on the grass.
Lina kicks the ball. Whoosh! It rolls and rolls.
The ball rolls to the edge of the street!
Oh no! The ball! Let's run and get it!
No, Adams! Stop! We never run into the street.
Adams stops. Lina stops. Milo stops too.
Stop means do not move. Stay where you are. Say it: stop!
Lina and Adams wait, and they call Mama.
Mama, our ball is near the street. Can you help us, please?
Mama looks left, and she looks right. No cars are coming.
The little man on the light turns green.
Green means go. Now it is safe to walk. Say it with me: go!
Mama gets the ball and comes back. Hooray!
Thank you, Mama! Thank you, Lina, for saying stop.
Now Adams rides his bike on the park path.
Go slow, Adams! There are little children here.
Okay! Slow, slow, slow. Like a little turtle!
Slow means not fast. Slow is careful and safe.
Can you say it? Slow!
Then Lina rides the bike, slowly too. They take turns.
Meow! I am slow too. I like to walk.
The sun is going down. It is time to go home.
Lina and Adams hold Mama's hands on the street.
I see a car, and a bus, and a bike!
At the corner, we stop. When the light is green, we go.
They walk slowly and carefully. Step, step, step.
We are safe on the street!
Milo walks with them all the way home. Meow!
At night, Lina and Adams are in the bedroom.
Today I saw a red car and a long yellow bus!
And you rode your bike with your helmet on.
You said stop, and you saved our day. Thank you, Lina.
Friends help friends to stay safe.
Milo curls up on the bed and closes his eyes.
Good night, Milo. Good night, Adams.
Good night, everyone!
